I feel duped. I should have bought the base game first, and not all the addons, but the reviews fooled me. The game has only one positive, and that is it's appealing visuals, at first glance, but now that I've played 50+ levels, including a bunch of DLC levels, I can safely say this shooter is severely flawed and not worth any price. Why:
1 The levels are near empty, and crazy repetative. 
2. There are maybe 10 levels, which are re-used in all 5000+ levels. 
3. The levels are short, very short.
4. There are only 2 level-types have 'surroundings' so permanent structures which stay, and the rest of all the levels is empty, so just enemies circling. Sure sometimes the background changes a bit, but there is no surrounding, they're empty levels. The surroundings the game does have are really, really badly designed: contact means instant death, and it's hard to see where the 'structure' ends and the background begins; it's all very blurry, and you'll often find yourself magically dying by 'bumping' into the structure, which popped out of now-where from the bottom of the screen (so not coming from the scrolling-direction of where the enemies come from).
5. There are but 4 types of enemies across all levels; outside of a boss there are no interesting enemies to speak of, they repeat the same 4 types with every level: a couple of 'streams' of flimsy enemies, sometimes a bigger round ball that has extremely predictable lame movement, and sometimes some jellyfish that slowly crosses the screen diagonally with no attack pattern whatsoever, followed by the end of each level: a boss. The levels are short, real short. 
6. The bosses are 'boring' in the sense that they have a few moves , and these simply rotate, but the pattern never evolves: they don't change their pattern or attack types after a certain amount of damage like virtually all other games with bossfight. 
7. There is no evolution; you can't gather anything that adds permanent upgrades to your ship.
8. The sound is simply crap. Hitting something, not hitting something, I can't tell the difference. And for that matter: 
9. Damage: how much (more) damage you do after a powerup? No idea, everything dies quickly really, except the boss. How much life the boss has left? No idea, no indicator, nothing, it just takes long or short depending on the 'level-difficulty'. 
It's just a plain bad side-scroller.
This game does not begin to compare in any way, shape or form with some of the great scroller-shooters like Sky Force, Xenon II, etc.

It's arcade action. So if you don't get driven to replay shmups and break high scores then you might not be satisfied with what's offered here. I enjoy it. And for the sale price of $12.50 I'd say it's very much worth it. I need more Darius in my life even if I suck at these games. And it's a great way to get more use out of my ultrawide monitor : )

I also like the DLC offerings here, something I rarely care for due to marketing practices of companies ever since DLC started becoming standard. But here we get some unique ships from other game series to have a try at. Good deal.

Dariusburst is a port AND a new game at the same time, it brings to PC the entire arcade experience (sadly the game is missing the Another Chronicle EX+ upgrade that allows you to use the Murakumo on that mode and the online events that the arcade had and are available on the switch version), on the other side Chronicle Saviours is a full new gamemode with 186 missions and 9 different ships to choose from; As of writing this review I've clocked 97hrs and I'm still nowhere near fully clearing CS mode so there's a lot for you to do.

Gameplay wise this is a honest shoot'em up with it's unique mechanic being the Burst weapon that you can either use as a fixed laser that will hit anything in a straight line from it's fixed position or forgo your normal shot and use a focused burst beam that has a special interaction with the burst beams of your enemy and that is counterbursting, which actually rewards practice and patience to master it as you not only get a damage boost but a higher score multiplier when killing enemies including bosses.

History, and yes there is one a long but at the same time short story, ACEX is a 32:9 retelling of Second Prologue's story and mostly just another side of the war BUT Chronicle Saviours is a straight continuation of the story from the PSP game Dariusburst (2009), specifically Ending 3(vs Syvalion) and pretty much is the culmination of a war that has been intermittenly happening for close to 2 millenia against the Belsar, althought hard to piece together if you only play CS and forgo all other games you will not miss anything outside of cameos/lore drops of the older games MCs; If you have played the PSP version OR SP you will get to see the fate of both MCs (kinda).

Onto the music, and what can I tell you it is ZUNTATA once again, you even get to hear all the songs from the older games on all stages that you get to use those ships. I will truly never get tired of hearing One Down between stages with the Genesis or SELF during a final boss with the Gaien.

DLCs... well they are totally optional you can't play with the ships/characters from each DLC on ACEX or CS mode so... yeah, the guidebook is a really cool addition tho I recommend it if you want to know extra stuff about the games, sadly it is not translated for some reason nor is it available as a PDF/EPUB.

As a final note, to this day remote play is broken and you WILL need to plug in an extra control if you want someone else to play with, and this increases by 1 for every other player. Thankfully there's a workaround via x360ce or any other controller emulator, you just need to fake that you have 4 controllers plugged in whenever you want to remote play (the other person MUST use a controller).

"Hey, Mikey?"

"Yeah?"

"Whaddya think woulda happened if 'R-Type Final' was actually 'Darius?'"

"I think it would have been something like 'DARIUSBURST Chronicle Saviours,' Paulie."

Or, to restate, it was shortly after I started playing this that I thought, "This is Taito's 'R-Type Final.'" Although, with less variety of ship choice, and a different graphical style. But some of the similarities were pretty eerie.

"DARChroSav" is definitely an arcade port. It's meant to be a devourer of quarters - guaranteed to kill you repeatedly until you've memorized everything, though easily defanged if you have unlimited continues. The graphics and enemy designs are pretty neat, but you won't get much time to look at anything because of all the projectiles you have to dodge. (That's just the way these things go.) The boss battles have a good dose of interest, but they also boil down to hammering a bullet sponge for several minutes. Of course, you can spend enough time to really learn all the patterns, but I don't find memorization to be all that fun.

The game promises a gazillion missions, and I certainly don't expect all of that to be handcrafted, but the content remixing got very samey in a hurry. There was also significant "clunk" factor, where finishing a mission in a certain mode dumps you all the way back into a primary menu, instead of letting you continue on with another zone as one might expect. That, in particular, seemed to be a strange choice to me.

Is this fun? Sure, it's a game I could have enjoyed in an arcade and also appreciated on my own PC. But 3 hours of it was plenty.

In this Shoot 'Em Up, you pilot a range of different small ships (all prefixed with the designation of "Silver Hawk") to take on an intergalactic army of what seems to be autonomous robot ships affiliated with the invading faction of Belser. The bosses and captains are all based on aquatic life, and their attack patterns—which are telegraphed with very fluid animations—reflect their respective inspirations quite nicely.

For anyone new to the game, I highly recommend you start with the CS Mode, making a genuine effort to complete it. Aside from the DLC mode, which is egregiously pricy for what it offers, the CS Mode is the *only* mode tailoured specifically for a single-player experience on a regular 16:9 monitor, and it has a more intuitive difficulty curve than the likes of Chronicle Mode or Original Mode EX. Every single level is perfectly beatable with the preset ships once you get the hang of their mechanics (especially the useful Fixed Burst); but you also have the option of spending your accumulated points on a custom ship selection, meaning you can start the level with up to 99 ARM (i.e. shields) and maxed shot/missile power. The only caveats are that your score won't be recorded on the global leaderboard, and that it's a bit too easy to trivialise the game by doing this, so try not to grow too dependent on it.

The game also offers a port of Another Chronicle EX, accessed by clicking on "AC Mode" in the main menu. But, being a port of an arcade release, it isn't quite as accessible. The huge 32:9 aspect ratio, letterboxing, scoring system being built for a local network, etc. makes it a bit of a harder sell. It's still worth checking out, as bosses like Dual Spin and Dreadful Whip are exclusive to this port, but CS Mode is the main appeal here.

Dariusburst's other noteworthy selling point is its soundtrack, produced by Zuntata, Taito's in-house band for the Darius series. Although primarily synthetic, it incorporates environmental samples, vocals, orchestral and Japanese instrumentation, percussion and so on to invoke a profound, contemplative feeling in the player. Some of my favourite tracks include "World of Spirit", "Hello 31337", "Kannanshinku", "You'll be in my thoughts", "Abyssal Holic", and "Syvalion arrange MMIX". 

In general, this game looks and plays great, with a lot of cool bosses and challenging stages, though I have some minor grips. One of the generic enemy types, called "Fena" (which look like a fusion between urchins and sea mines) is extremely obnoxious whenever it appears — which is often. Unlike virtually every other enemy in the game, Fena materialise *on-screen* in an erratic fashion. This often means that they will spawn inside your ship's hurtbox unpredictably, meaning you'll take damage through no fault of your own. This is not fair at all: an enemy like this should always have a delayed hitbox or a screen effect that telegraphs their spawning coordinates so you can take evasive action. Also, it's impossible to exit to the main menu in AC Mode, since every keyboard and controller input is treated as either a selection or confirmation button, meaning you're forced to close and relaunch the game to access other modes from there.

Dariusburst Chronicle Saviours is an excellent game, even for someone who has barely engaged with Shmups before. The usual £42.00 price tag is somewhat steep, but as of making this review, it's currently on sale with a 70% discount, which is a steal. Check it out if you want a game you can boot up whenever and get the same mileage out of it each time.

I think The Electric Underground said it best in his DDP DOJ rerelease overview. Something along the lines of “you can *feel* the quality in a game by touching it despite its age, an enemy doesn’t just blow up, it explodes into a dozen little pieces with different sizes for every enemy. Everything is (touched up) to make you feel good.”

Dariusburst did not feel that way. I’m being less harsh on it because it was a genuine desire to revive the series that created the original PSP title, but if this were to come out at any other time then it would be called almost gacha-tier grind nostalgia slop like dodonpachi maximum or gothic wa mahou otome. 

There was more expression in games aged 20 years before it (Dariusburst is 2009) on things like… even just an animation for turning the ship around in G Darius. Not just sprite flipping. All of the text is an ugly default document font in bold letters. The stages have an alright, if not very memorable design, but they’re ruined by being reused ad infinitum and you get sick of looking at any of them after twenty minutes. Enemies disappear with a wet fart compared to how visceral G Darius was. Everything in this game feels exactly what it is; a bland PSP revival title (of which there are MANY) on several dozen add on packs to try to keep it on life support instead of properly updating the core game and enhancing it after all these years. No, just adding more numbers to all the existing stages to reuse them is not enhancing or updating; it’s padding. I had the most fun using the DLC ships in their *one* mode called DLC Mode, but in the end I was doing the same thing to them. Playing a hollow shell version of those games instead of just playing those games.

セール中に購入し、一気に４時間もプレイしてしまいました。シリーズはツイン→外伝→Gダラとプレイして参りましたが、過去一面白いかもしれません。設置バーストの使い方がわかってくると一気に楽しく、爽快感が溢れ出ます。こんなに自由度の高い戦い方ができるシューティングゲームは初めてです。機体も沢山あるので、いろんなプレイが出来そうでワクワクします。音楽も素晴らしく、特にアーケードモードのシームレスな音楽とＳＥとのハーモニーで脳汁ドバドバです。

かつて自分の思い出としてはＧダラの作り込まれた世界観と、オシャレな音楽、ボス戦の演出に感動し、これ以上シューティングゲームで感動する経験はできないのではないかと思っておりましたが、Ｇダラ以来の感動です。流石はダライアス！

グラフィックは流石に今プレイすると数世代前の画質と感じ、そしてＧダラのような緻密な演出が感じられなかった点は残念でした。ですがプレイの爽快感と楽しさは、自分にとっていまだかつてないものです。更に、デュアルディスプレイでアーケードモードをプレイした時は大迫力で感動しました。

ＣＳモードもマップを進めていく感じが楽しく、じっくり遊べそうです。そして何より、プリセットならばミッションごとに機体数の縛りがあり、難易度設定やコンティニューなどの緩和要素が無いところが逆に燃えてきます。悔しい、やられた！ならばこうやって攻略してみようか、と自分なりに工夫して、クリアできたときはガッツポーズが出てしまいました。某死にゲー的な歯ごたえがあって楽しいです。

素晴らしいゲームを作って下さってありがとうございました。そして、プレイするのが今更というタイミングで申し訳ございませんが、これから毎日楽しくプレイさせて頂きます。いずれダライアスの新作シリーズも期待しております！
